claim.claim-text: 2. The surgical instrument of claim 1, further comprising an outer sheath, having a length, and connected to the cap, the outer sheath rotatable about the length direction thereof.

3. The surgical instrument of claim 1 or 2, the first flexible member further including a first member manipulator having a first member length, the first member manipulator rotatable about its length direction and translationally movable with respect to the length direction, and the first flexible member is bendable by the first manipulator.

4. The surgical instrument of claim 1, 2 or 3, wherein the cap further comprises a third aperture therethrough, and an imaging member is selectively extendable and retractable with respect to the third aperture.

5. The surgical instrument of claim 4, wherein the outer sheath is a flexible sheath having a first flexible sheath connected to the first aperture of the cap and a second flexible sheath connected to the second aperture of the cap.

6. The surgical instrument of claim 5, wherein the first flexible member is translationally movable within or outwardly from the first flexible sheath by the first member manipulator with respect to the length direction of the first flexible sheath.
7. The surgical instrument of claim 5, wherein the first flexible member is rotationally movable by the first member manipulator about the length direction of the first flexible sheath.

8. The surgical instrument of claim 4, wherein the cap further comprises a first portion through which the first and second apertures extend, and an extending portion through which the third aperture extends.

9. The surgical instrument of claim 5, further comprising an instrument handle connected to the outer sheath at a first end thereof, and a first introduction port located distal of the first end thereon, wherein the first flexible member is extendable therethrough, and linearly movable inwardly and outwardly of, and rotatable with respect to, the first introduction port.
10. The surgical instrument of claim 1, wherein:
the first end effector extends in a first end effector direction; and the first end effector direction is positionable at a single or a double angle with respect to the first flexible member.
11. A method of positioning an end effector with respect to a cap on the end of a sheath, comprising:

12. The method of claim 11, further comprising moving the first flexible member in the length direction of the sheath to extend the first arm, the second arm, and the first end effector outwardly of the cap.
13. The method of claim 11, further comprising rotating the first flexible member about the length direction of the sheath.
14. The method of claim 11, further comprising providing a second end effector on the fourth arm.
